name: Fitbod
why: AI strength app whose workouts are built around a per-muscle recovery percentage; its own help center (updated 2026-09-15) says recovery 'is an estimate, not a measurement' and that it only sees what is logged or pulled from Apple Health/Health Connect. Multi-device already (Apple Watch, Wear OS, Fitbit, Strava, BLE heart-rate straps incl. Garmin/Polar/WHOOP broadcast), and a named partnerships lead (Jesse Padilla) owns B2B and partner relationships.
why_now: Recovery help article updated 2026-09-15; Fitbod for Business page updated 2026-06-17 says it is 'open to discussing partnerships'.
warm_path: Contact: Jesse Padilla, Senior Head of Sales & Partnerships (source: https://www.linkedin.com/in/jesse-padilla-30582032)
ask: 15-minute call with partnerships/product on adding overnight HRV + sleep as an optional input to the muscle-recovery model; offer a DevKit slot.
opener: Hi Jesse, I'm the founder of Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. We're building a screenless band worn overnight that records ECG-based HRV and sleep data, with an open SDK and no subscription. Fitbod's help center calls recovery an estimate built from logged workouts. Would a measured overnight signal be useful as an optional input? We're choosing 5-10 DevKit design partners this fall. Open to 15 minutes?
existing_wearables: Bluetooth LE heart rate monitors (Garmin, Polar, WHOOP broadcast)
opportunity: Vybe writes overnight HRV/sleep to HealthKit/Health Connect (which Fitbod already reads for activity) and pitches Fitbod to read those fields, or a direct SDK feed, so a low-readiness night nudges the muscle-recovery percentages or swaps in lower-intensity movements for today's workout; co-market to Fitbod's strength users.
unknowns: Whether Fitbod reads HRV/sleep from HealthKit today (docs list workouts, energy, heart rate, body composition only); appetite for new data sources; size of partnerships team; any API terms.

NY company with $45M total funding per its founder's LinkedIn, now selling into studios.
why_now: 2026-07-24 LinkedIn post launching studio/commercial channel (Core Collective) and inviting studios to reach its commercial team.
ask: Intro call with product (founder or CPO) on adding Vybe as a sleep/recovery source next to Apple Health and Oura; offer a DevKit unit.
opener: Hi Shalom, I'm the founder of Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. amp's site says each night of sleep shapes how much resistance you get the next day. We're building a screenless band worn overnight that captures ECG-based HRV and sleep, licensed through an SDK, no subscription. Could Vybe sit next to Apple Health and Oura as a recovery source? We have 5-10 DevKit design-partner slots. Worth a short call?
opportunity: Add Vybe as a third overnight recovery source feeding amp's 'energized vs not' resistance and workout personalization; also a studio angle (amp commercial studios) for band pilots with members.
unknowns: Exact integration method (HealthKit vs Oura API) and which metrics amp actually reads; whether amp builds integrations for small/pre-launch devices; no public partner page found (commercial email is only published for studio sales).

name: Peloton

Reporting on a March 2026 Bloomberg piece says Peloton is building a 'Daily Suggested Workout' from smartwatch/ring recovery data.
why_now: Q4 FY26 earnings call (reported 2026-08-12): 'a couple more big ones on the way'; readiness-based daily workout in development.
warm_path: Contact: Brad Fagan, VP, Global Head of Strategic Partnerships & Corporate Development (source: https://www.linkedin.com/in/brad-fagan-8382a888)
ask: Find the Peloton IQ / wearables-partnerships owner via LinkedIn or a warm intro and ask for a 20-minute intro once DevKit data is shareable; realistic near-term goal is being on the list for a later integration wave.

unknowns: No public partner/developer program or contact found; the named partnerships owner is unknown; whether Peloton reads HRV/sleep from Apple Health today; the 'Daily Suggested Workout' has no launch date.

name: Caliber
why: Strength-training app plus paid 1:1 human coaching (NYC, ~40-60 staff). It syncs activity via Apple Health and Health Connect (Garmin routed through Apple Health) and has no direct wearable integration yet. Its public feature board shows users asking for a WHOOP integration, a direct Garmin integration ('Planned') and a 'Caliber API' (under consideration), and lists 'Suggested workout changes' as under consideration, so recovery data is in demand.
why_now: Feature board active in 2026: the 'Caliber API' idea was posted 10 Feb by co-founder Chris Muir; Health Connect support shipped 2024-07-31.
warm_path: Contact: Chris Muir, Co-Founder & CPO (source: https://www.linkedin.com/in/chris-muir)
ask: 15-minute call with Chris Muir on giving Caliber coaches a nightly HRV/sleep view for clients who wear a Vybe band; DevKit pilot with a few coaches.
opener: Hi Chris, I'm the founder of Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. I saw Caliber members asking for WHOOP and Garmin integrations on your feature board. We're building a screenless band worn overnight that records ECG-based HRV and sleep, with an SDK and no subscription. Could a few Caliber coaches pilot it to see clients' overnight data next to their training log? We're picking 5-10 design partners. Open to 15 minutes?
opportunity: Coach-facing pilot: Caliber coaches see a client's overnight HRV/sleep trend (via HealthKit/Health Connect or Vybe API) and adjust that week's program; later, feed the planned 'suggested workout changes' feature. Co-market to the free-app audience.
unknowns: Whether Caliber reads sleep/HRV from Apple Health today; whether the Garmin/WHOOP items moved since 2022; no partner page; the 2026 date on the 'Caliber API' idea is shown as '10 Feb' without a year, so it is inferred.

name: Simple Muscle
why: Brand-new iPhone strength tracker (launched 2026-08-10) built so the user's own AI assistant (ChatGPT/Claude via MCP) writes the plan and reads training history. No wearable or Apple Health integration appears on its site; it exposes plans, sets and history only. A recovery signal is the missing context for 'adjust today's workout', and the solo founder ships fast and posts publicly on LinkedIn.
why_now: App launched 2026-08-10 (founder LinkedIn post); MCP connector live in Claude per its site (Aug 2026).
warm_path: Both are MCP-native: Vybe's API/MCP plus Simple Muscle's MCP can be demoed together in one Claude chat
ask: Joint MCP demo: Claude reads last night's Vybe HRV/sleep plus Simple Muscle history and updates today's template; DevKit unit for the founder.
opener: Hi Vladimir, I'm the founder of Vybe Health in Akron, Ohio. I love the idea behind Simple Muscle: the assistant plans, the app just tracks. We're building a screenless band worn overnight that records ECG-based HRV and sleep, with an SDK, no subscription. If an assistant could read last night's data next to your history, it could adjust today's template. Want a DevKit to try a joint demo?
opportunity: Be the first wearable signal in the Simple Muscle loop, either by adding an Apple Health/Vybe read or simply by pairing Vybe's API/MCP with Simple Muscle's MCP in the same assistant so readiness adjusts today's workout; co-publish the demo.
unknowns: No wearable/HealthKit integration found, but not confirmed absent (so existing_wearables=null); tiny user base; founder location not verified; whether it is a side project or a business.
